The Silver Exchange

Elias smoothed his uniform in the lobby’s silver mirror, finding comfort in his steady gaze during the lonely shift. Fiction.

Mr. Vane approached the desk, his heavy coat drinking the light as he leaned forward to sign the register.

Behind him, the grand mirror showed only the empty hallway; there was no guest visible in the glass.

"The mirror never lies," Elias whispered, his fingers trembling as he slid the key across the cold marble.

Vane looked up with weary eyes and a thin smile that didn't reach his reflective, silver pupils.

"I’ve been looking for a fresh perspective," the guest murmured, his hand brushing Elias’s skin with a freezing touch.

Elias turned back to the glass and gasped as his own reflection began to fade into a gray mist.

In its place, Vane’s image solidified in the silver, leaving Elias standing there as a formless shadow.

The mirror never lies.
